Debug analysis by Netra below Error seen on pxp1/port0 on both socket 0 and 1. >>> sls() ============================================= SOCKET0  ============================================= PXP0 is x16 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- PXP1 is x8 -- -- -- x2 x2 x2 x2 PXP2 is x16 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- PXP3 is x16 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- PXP4 is x4 -- x4 -- x4 -- x4 -- PXP5 is x4 -- x4 -- x4 -- x4 -- ===== Port pxp0.port0 (PCIE/rp0/fbrp0) is x16 (ilw=x16) (dllla=1) (GEN5/dP5/uP9). LTSSM = UP_L0 Port pxp1.port0 (PCIE/rp0/fbrp0) is x0  (ilw=x0) (dllla=0) (GEN1/-3.5dB). LTSSM = DET_QUIET_RST   ==> pxp1/rp0 Port pxp1.port2 (PCIE/rp2/fbrp4) is x1  (ilw=x1) (dllla=1) (GEN1/-3.5dB). LTSSM = UP_L0 This corresponds to below pcie topology and IOMCA would be reported with this root port's B/D/F (0x29:0x:00) 29:00.0 System peripheral: Intel Corporation Ice Lake Memory Map/VT-d 29:00.1 System peripheral: Intel Corporation Ice Lake Mesh 2 PCIe 29:00.2 System peripheral: Intel Corporation Ice Lake RAS 29:00.4 Generic system peripheral [0807]: Intel Corporation Device 0b23 29:06.0 PCI bridge: Intel Corporation Device 0db2 29:07.0 PCI bridge: Intel Corporation Device 0db8 29:08.0 PCI bridge: Intel Corporation Device 0db3 29:09.0 PCI bridge: Intel Corporation Device 0db9 Since, the B/D/F is not enumerated, am not sure what is connected there. However, we could also try re-seating the device to see if it gets detected. This detect problems exists on pxp1/port0 of both sockets. While there are 2 devices failing to get detected always. They may not necessarily cause the system to hang. Recommend marking this sighting as root caused. Root cause is attributed to thermal shutdown of PCIe devices leading to SLD event and IOMCA. Next steps: 1) Experiments to prevent device thermal shutdown based on recommendations from system thermal team a) Enhance airflow with additional opening of chassis air ducts b) Thermally optimal placement of PCIe AICs without crossing thermal limits on closed chassis AVC and BNC systems. 2) Discussion with BMC team on monitoring PCIe AIC temperatures 3) Enhance PCIe error telemetry in cluster - discussions with data science team

Update on next steps: 1. BKM identified for optimal placement of PCIe cards in MAX I/O config based on thermal report for AVC and BNC platform to avoid hitting PCIe AIC thermal thresholds - wiki - BHS closed chassis Max IO BKM 2. Include PCIe AIC temperatures into BMC FSC algorithm a) Based on PoC with BMC team, PLDM feature in BMC can be used for thermal monitoring of riser card and PCIe AICs (except RPB test card) via IPMI on AVC and BNC﻿. wiki - BHS PCIe AIC card temp monitoring using PLDM b) CCB exists to support this on OKS platform Thermal handling - AIC / HSBP drives - Temperature input to FSC algorithm.  Supporting this on BHS require thermal modeling on AVC and BNC. c) Submit feature request to RPB team to support temp monitoring (requires business justification) d) Submit feature request to expose all PLDM temp sensor data via Redfish 3. Enhance PCIe error telemetry in BHS cluster a) JIRA submitted to add PCIe UNCERRSTS register into collector service - [SPIVAUTO-2189] Add PCIE ERRUNCSTS register to ras collector for BHS and EGS Recommend closing this HSD.

comments_structured.text: Current findings, with IOMCA disabled we are able to recreate the issue. The reason for UBOX error is due to Surprise Link down (SLD) which is fatal error causing UBOX. In PLR2 this SLD due to this change https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14024202855  it was made as a FATAL error. In PLR1, this SLD error was non-fatal. We are checking with PLR1 if any SLD was seen and not flagged as an error. Will keep posted on what we find based on the test results. Thanks to  @Sg, Roopesh for pointing to SLD failure with IOMCA disabled.

comments_structured.author: diegog3
comments_structured.text: Hi all, As you may know there was a request to enable SLD in BIOS https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article-one/#/article/22020433270 Shindo, Miki Last updated on: Thursday, January 16, 20255:59:11 PM(a month ago) id:  14613703589 CN All The patch has been merged to PB2.  Thanks! BCHSTRM.0.RPB.3544.P.36 will pick the patch.  Adding PB2_MERGED tag. Just to make it clear unmasking this error by default was to notify the system immediately about a device that goes down and prevent data corruption or unexpected behaviors in the platform, keep in mind that the severity of the issue is fatal and without contention mechanisms like DPC a system reboot to recover from that failure is expected.  What is not expected is to have a device going down when running stress tests on it, the next step of dumping the AER registers at the time of the failure is good next debug step. If confirmed that the system is signaling a SLD error that should be the focus of this debug.

comments_structured.text: Pasting more relevant temperature updates from the Teams about MLX: Avelar, Omar: I would physically go check the nodes to inspect: cooling / air-flow, and bump+fix the fan-speed to the max, and anything that can alleviate over-temps  So the RPB has no commercial OS driver, you will not get proper feedback if it's over-temp also and causing a card shutdown/SLD, it might not be obvious.... but Puthenpurackal Rajappan, Jayaraj might have a backdoor he can check or an on-die temp sensor for RPB to poll  For now, we know the HSD is intertwined with the RPB & Mellanox - but the mlx NIC is at least claiming over-temp and giving us a clear reason: 2025-02-21T09:54:35.740425000Z,[  574.124900] mlx5_core 0000:b8:00.0: print_health_info:421:(pid 0): Health issue observed, High temperature, severity(2) CRITICAL:  Fan-curves, air-flow obstruction, check that physically.... max IO setups are known to restrict airflow if not done beautifully. Puthenpurackal Rajappan, Jayaraj: BTW, mining through BHS cluster telemetry data, we figured that MLX cards on these Max IO configs have been reporting over temp errors since quite some time (for now we checked for last 3 months or so, but can try to go back even further)    Post the recent change to unmask SLD AER, we are likely noticing these errors now due to fatal IOMCA when SLD error occurs due to over temp conditions. Nelsen, Pau: MellanoxCX7_manual.pdf Per the manual, 3 inches of clearance and max ambient temp 55oC.  Are we meeting those requirements in the cluster?    Ye, Jun Y: That is how the device/link is managed if thermal is involved.

comments_structured.author: jputhenp
comments_structured.text: Recommend marking this sighting as root caused. Root cause is attributed to thermal shutdown of PCIe devices leading to SLD event and IOMCA. Next steps: 1) Experiments to prevent device thermal shutdown based on recommendations from system thermal team a) Enhance airflow with additional opening of chassis air ducts b) Thermally optimal placement of PCIe AICs without crossing thermal limits on closed chassis AVC and BNC systems. 2) Discussion with BMC team on monitoring PCIe AIC temperatures 3) Enhance PCIe error telemetry in cluster - discussions with data science team

comments_structured.author: jputhenp
comments_structured.text: Update on next steps: 1. BKM identified for optimal placement of PCIe cards in MAX I/O config based on thermal report for AVC and BNC platform to avoid hitting PCIe AIC thermal thresholds - wiki - BHS closed chassis Max IO BKM 2. Include PCIe AIC temperatures into BMC FSC algorithm a) Based on PoC with BMC team, PLDM feature in BMC can be used for thermal monitoring of riser card and PCIe AICs (except RPB test card) via IPMI on AVC and BNC﻿. wiki - BHS PCIe AIC card temp monitoring using PLDM b) CCB exists to support this on OKS platform Thermal handling - AIC / HSBP drives - Temperature input to FSC algorithm.  Supporting this on BHS require thermal modeling on AVC and BNC. c) Submit feature request to RPB team to support temp monitoring (requires business justification) d) Submit feature request to expose all PLDM temp sensor data via Redfish 3. Enhance PCIe error telemetry in BHS cluster a) JIRA submitted to add PCIe UNCERRSTS register into collector service - [SPIVAUTO-2189] Add PCIE ERRUNCSTS register to ras collector for BHS and EGS Recommend closing this HSD.

raw.bug.fix_description:
Update on next steps:



1. BKM identified for optimal placement of PCIe cards in MAX I/O config based on thermal report for AVC and BNC platform to avoid hitting PCIe AIC thermal thresholds - wiki - BHS closed chassis Max IO BKM

2. Include PCIe AIC temperatures into BMC FSC algorithm
a) Based on PoC with BMC team, PLDM feature in BMC can be used for thermal monitoring of riser card and PCIe AICs (except RPB test card) via IPMI on AVC and BNC﻿. wiki - BHS PCIe AIC card temp monitoring using PLDM
b) CCB exists to support this on OKS platform Thermal handling - AIC / HSBP drives - Temperature input to FSC algorithm.  Supporting this on BHS require thermal modeling on AVC and BNC.
c) Submit feature request to RPB team to support temp monitoring (requires business justification)
d) Submit feature request to expose all PLDM temp sensor data via Redfish

3. Enhance PCIe error telemetry in BHS cluster

a) JIRA submitted to add PCIe UNCERRSTS register into collector service - [SPIVAUTO-2189] Add PCIE ERRUNCSTS register to ras collector for BHS and EGS

Recommend closing this HSD.

articles.title: [IPS 14023496267] [AMI] System hang for 4 mins while chanaging HW GPIO from VGPIO & NMI Button press
articles.description: configuration used: OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Platform: Beechnut CIty platform SRF SP Q4VY CPU CPLD: WW50 BMC: WW50 BIOS label: 3544P24 Reproduction steps Step 1. Boot to Ubuntu 22.04 OS. Step 2. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 3. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO Step 4. Push the NMI button. Step 5. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS Step 6. Change to VGPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 7. To check the current setting is VGPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 Step 8. Push the NMI button. Step 9. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS Step 10. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 11. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO Step 12. Push the NMI button. Step 13. System will hang on about 2min with Intel and AMI BIOS This issue is not reproduced with IFWI binary provided on SRF-SP BKC, this issue happens with a IFWI image generated by BIOS code from Intel Github OTCShare repository ----------------------------------------------------------- original customer request ----------------------------------------------------------- while changing HW GPIO from VGPIO we can observe system hang for about 4mins after pressing NMI button with Intel RC built BIOS (RC3085.M14). Case 1: Setting HWGPIO (PASS) Case 2: HWGPIO to VGPIO (PASS) Case 3: VGPIO to HWGPIO (FAIL) with case 3 , the system hang is observed along with system locked.When tried to change the GPIO from VGPIO to HGPIO, the system has hanged for about ~4 minutes. After 4 minutes tried to take dmesg for the failure case, but the system automatically locked

Taskforce Update: S3M RTL bug identified to be incorrectly asserting the IOCHK_STS flag on ESPI NMI events.  When the IOCHK NMI was broadcast to all cores through a HW NMI path the BSP was being stalled for 2 seconds per core, this 2 seconds * number of cores (144 cores in our case) would be the 4 to 5 minutes to completely go through all of the cores The debug found that these 2 second stalls was also causing some cores to watchdog and transition to either Soft_Lockup or Hard_Lockup states.  When the Watchdog events happen on the core running the console window the user would experience a non-responsive system When the Watchdog event happened on BSP core then the OS would become truly hung.  Also during this debug it was discovered that further ESPI NMIs (after the first) were being blocked because the flow was not documented for any agent to 'deassert' the NMI in the ITSS. The debug uncovered an issue with the main FPGA having incorrect polarity on the ESPI NMIs and was confirmed with ESPI trace capture indicating a deassert followed by a assert packet, leaving the IPs in an asserted state as default. Workarounds       UPLR1:   IOCHK never to be generated, and correct the polarity of the ESPI vWire NMIs ·       Fixes AMI / Gigabyte hangs on HW NMIs (after an ESPI NMI) ·       Fixes Oracle initial HSD issue with OS - Core 0 (BIOS assigned core 0 / BSP) routing ·       Fixes “potential issues” with OSs that attempt port 70 NMI reasserts ·       Multiple HW NMIs functional, Multiple ESPI NMIs still broken 1: S3M FW patch will keep the internal ITSS version of NMI_STS_CNT.IOCHK_NMI_EN always set to 1 to disable any sources of IOCHK since there are no IOCHK sources in S3M.  At the same time FW will keep a local copy of this register bit for host SW to access that will maintain the R/W attribute per spec.   2: The FPGA will correct the NMI polarity into the ESPI wrapper internally      UPLR2:    Correct the multiple NMIs on ESPI by clearing (de-asserting) the NMI in the ITSS                              ·       Fixes AMI requirement for multiple NMIs on ESPI 1:  S3M FW patch will forward the ESPI de-assert to the ITSS as an NMI de-assert. ·       AR:  Blaine/Kurt S.: Since this was reference code provided and may have duplicated this portion of code in the CPLDs, we need to have an MOW published to inform customers of this change in the FPGA?

comments_structured.text: Taskforce Update: S3M RTL bug identified to be incorrectly asserting the IOCHK_STS flag on ESPI NMI events.  When the IOCHK NMI was broadcast to all cores through a HW NMI path the BSP was being stalled for 2 seconds per core, this 2 seconds * number of cores (144 cores in our case) would be the 4 to 5 minutes to completely go through all of the cores The debug found that these 2 second stalls was also causing some cores to watchdog and transition to either Soft_Lockup or Hard_Lockup states.  When the Watchdog events happen on the core running the console window the user would experience a non-responsive system When the Watchdog event happened on BSP core then the OS would become truly hung.  Also during this debug it was discovered that further ESPI NMIs (after the first) were being blocked because the flow was not documented for any agent to 'deassert' the NMI in the ITSS. The debug uncovered an issue with the main FPGA having incorrect polarity on the ESPI NMIs and was confirmed with ESPI trace capture indicating a deassert followed by a assert packet, leaving the IPs in an asserted state as default. Workarounds       UPLR1:   IOCHK never to be generated, and correct the polarity of the ESPI vWire NMIs ·       Fixes AMI / Gigabyte hangs on HW NMIs (after an ESPI NMI) ·       Fixes Oracle initial HSD issue with OS - Core 0 (BIOS assigned core 0 / BSP) routing ·       Fixes “potential issues” with OSs that attempt port 70 NMI reasserts ·       Multiple HW NMIs functional, Multiple ESPI NMIs still broken 1: S3M FW patch will keep the internal ITSS version of NMI_STS_CNT.IOCHK_NMI_EN always set to 1 to disable any sources of IOCHK since there are no IOCHK sources in S3M.  At the same time FW will keep a local copy of this register bit for host SW to access that will maintain the R/W attribute per spec.   2: The FPGA will correct the NMI polarity into the ESPI wrapper internally      UPLR2:    Correct the multiple NMIs on ESPI by clearing (de-asserting) the NMI in the ITSS                              ·       Fixes AMI requirement for multiple NMIs on ESPI 1:  S3M FW patch will forward the ESPI de-assert to the ITSS as an NMI de-assert. ·       AR:  Blaine/Kurt S.: Since this was reference code provided and may have duplicated this portion of code in the CPLDs, we need to have an MOW published to inform customers of this change in the FPGA?

TITLE: [IPS 14023496267] [AMI] System hang for 4 mins while chanaging HW GPIO from VGPIO & NMI Button press

DESCRIPTION:
configuration used: OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Platform: Beechnut CIty platform SRF SP Q4VY CPU CPLD: WW50 BMC: WW50 BIOS label: 3544P24 Reproduction steps Step 1. Boot to Ubuntu 22.04 OS. Step 2. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 3. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO Step 4. Push the NMI button. Step 5. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS Step 6. Change to VGPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 7. To check the current setting is VGPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 Step 8. Push the NMI button. Step 9. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS Step 10. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 Step 11. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console: i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1 0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO Step 12. Push the NMI button. Step 13. System will hang on about 2min with Intel and AMI BIOS This issue is not reproduced with IFWI binary provided on SRF-SP BKC, this issue happens with a IFWI image generated by BIOS code from Intel Github OTCShare repository ----------------------------------------------------------- original customer request ----------------------------------------------------------- while changing HW GPIO from VGPIO we can observe system hang for about 4mins after pressing NMI button with Intel RC built BIOS (RC3085.M14). Case 1: Setting HWGPIO (PASS) Case 2: HWGPIO to VGPIO (PASS) Case 3: VGPIO to HWGPIO (FAIL) with case 3 , the system hang is observed along with system locked.When tried to change the GPIO from VGPIO to HGPIO, the system has hanged for about ~4 minutes. After 4 minutes tried to take dmesg for the failure case, but the system automatically locked

Step 2. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00


Step 3. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1


0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO

Step 4. Push the NMI button.

Step 5. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS

Step 6. Change to VGPIO method, key the command via BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00


Step 7. To check the current setting is VGPIO method, key command vi BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1


Step 8. Push the NMI button.

Step 9. System will not hang on about 2min with AMI BIOS. --> PASS

Step 10. To change to HW GPIO method, key the command via BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w6@0x51 0x40 0x30 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00


Step 11. To check the current setting is HW GPIO method, key command vi BMC console:

i2ctransfer -y 10 w2@0x51 0x40 0x30 r1


0 = VGPIO method, 1 ; HW GPIO

Step 12. Push the NMI button.

Step 13. System will hang on about 2min with Intel and AMI BIOS


This issue is not reproduced with IFWI binary provided on SRF-SP BKC, this issue happens with a IFWI image generated by BIOS code from Intel Github OTCShare repository




-----------------------------------------------------------

original customer request

-----------------------------------------------------------

while changing HW GPIO from VGPIO we can observe system hang for about 4mins after pressing NMI button with Intel RC built BIOS (RC3085.M14).


Case 1: Setting HWGPIO (PASS)

Case 2: HWGPIO to VGPIO (PASS)

Case 3: VGPIO to HWGPIO (FAIL)


with case 3 , the system hang is observed along with system locked.When tried to change the GPIO from VGPIO to HGPIO, the system has hanged for about ~4 minutes. After 4 minutes tried to take dmesg for the failure case, but the system automatically locked

articles.title: [SRF-SP-ROW][CXL] Remote Core to CXL Bandwidth degrade of 5-20% observed across 100NTW, 1R1W, 2R1W, 1R1NTW, 2R1NTW WLs in PLR1/PLR2
articles.description: Remote Core to CXL Bandwidth shows a degrade of 5-20% for W2,W5,W6, W7 and W8 KPIs as compared to Targets. Please refer to the Attachment - CXL_Remote_Final_HSD_v1.xlsx / 2_Tier-603_BKC97vsBKC98_Final, Core to CXL 2 Tier measurements. The measurements were done on both PLR1 and PLR2 and seeing similar degrades in both the Releases. System Name fl31ca103an0304.amr.corp.intel.com QDF RPG3 No of CXL Cards 4 (2 CXL cards each on Soc0 and Soc1) CXL Mode 2 Tier CXL Card Model Astera A0 CXL FW Version 1.3.0 FW Speed 5600 CXL DDR5 Size 64GB * 2 (1 DPC) Native DDR5 size 32GB * 8
comments: As part of the debug, have tried the following steps. Exp 1 : Tried the affected Remote KPIs on 3 different setups to confirm issue consistency :     System Issue observed?  % of Delta  Comments fl31ca103bs0603 Yes 3-20% This system was received from NPI as part of CXL transition fl41ca202js0403 Partially (for 100NTW, 2R1NTW, 1R1NTW) 2-5% This is NPI system that was used to publish the numbers in the NPI report fl31ca103an0304 Yes 3-20% Brought up the new system with CXL hardware from 603 system above to rule out system/CXL card problem Outcome :- Same CXL hardware on the different system with same BIOS/OS/other hardware peripherals shows the same issue. CXL Hardware could be the issue. Exp2: On the new setup fl31ca103an0304 tried the below : Used 304 system from above Experiment row No.3 and replaced 4 CXL cards (S0 and S1) Re-flashing the CXL FW  Enabling maximum cooling for the system to avoid thermal throttling.   Outcome :- Still see 3-20% delta for all Workloads. This means with 2 systems and 2 different sets of CXL cards we are seeing the problem. Exp3: Check soc1 local core to CXL path      W2 S0  S1  NPI Score Local Core to CXL 147 135 142   Outcome :- Soc1 local core to CXL not able to match Soc0 core to CXL. Hence suspecting issue with soc1 core to cxl path or soc1 connected CXL cards. Exp4:  Compare S0 to S1 and S1 to S0 Remote Bandwidth.     W2 S0 to S1 S1 to S0 NPI Data Remote Core to CXL 83 83.7 90   Outcome :- From Exp3 local S1 bandwidth shortfall does not seem to be affecting S0 to S1 vs S1 to S0.

When we received the system from NPI, the CXL cards FW version was 1.1, upgraded it to 1.3. Just to cross check went back to FW version 1.1 and ran the same Remote KPI measurements. Please see below table for the measurements Observations: 1. For most Workloads(except 100%NTW sequential and random) we recover the bandwidth with FW version 1.1 (compare col. L vs R) 2. With FW version 1.1 vs 1.3 local CXL to mem we do not see any large deltas (Please see attachment) 3. comments_structured.text: From the kernel logs, it appears that the GPF is happening in the function "arch_get_unmapped_area_uopdown" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.066163] CR2: 00007f76ac011000 CS3: 0000061fb8182002 CS4: 0000000008f70ee0" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.077346] Caml Trace;" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.097180]  ? arch_get_unmapped_area_uopdown+1x1ae/0x3c0" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.113541]  ? rwsem_optimistic_spin+0y88/0x171" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.082574]  ? die_addr+0x37/0y90" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.091720]  ? asm_exc_general_protection+0x26/0x30" "May 16, 2025 @ 19:04:58.557",fl31ca102fs0905,"[21062.086365]  ? exc_general_prouection+1x246/0x540" As per the kernel documentation, arch_get_unmapped_area_uopdown function is part of the Linux kernel's memory management system. This function is responsible for finding suitable memory locations that are not currently in use. A GPF within this function could be due to memory corruption due to kernel bug or faulty hardware. However, I would not suspect a kernel bug as this is not seen on other systems. Could be a fauly hardware as we are seeing few SMI handler messages. It would be better to check these SMI handler messages on working platforms also if possible we can replace the dimms on this platform and give a try.

comments: will need node for repro dimm reported CE storm during idle, 6hrs after lemon grass was done failed in near identical way to the Hynix MRDIMMs ( 15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ).  https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/5dfHHIaNk?orgId=1 RREL registers shows same 4DQ and around 32bit parity count and C4 Error class (same as MRDIMM idle fails) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/VlYsE4-Hz?orgId=1   same system failed back in Jan on a different dimm with same fail signature  @Lee, Caty let me know when the node is available.

Set SystemErrorEnable=0 and OS kernel parameter mcelog=off and let the node sit idle. System hit idle fails after ~10days of idle on separate dimm (CPU0 IMC5, SN 76C23D96) pythonsv logs attached fl31ca102gs0909_HynixRDimm-Renesas_Idle-CEStorm-CPU0IMC5_0612_pythonsv.zip Statusscope also captured 5e1bb603-26df-3ccf-4e0e-ac7b9b945985 - AxonSV - Record Viewer fail signature once again follows same 4DQ, 32 parity bit count, Error class C4 all Bank/bankgroup/Col/Row as the Hynix MRDimm idle issue as mentioned previously (15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/BzpX6EYHk?orgId=1  three different dimms have failed similarly in the past 6months on this node. Polling through historic data to see if there are more Hynix RDIMMs that have failed similarly.

There is strong evidence that the issue has been happening somewhat regularly on Hynix RDIMMs over the last 6 months. Repro rate is low and only two nodes have had repeated fails (though always on different dimms).  Below is the list of 4DQ fails in the cluster over the last 6 months. Each Vendor has ~4000-5000 dimms installed in the cluster

will need node for repro dimm reported CE storm during idle, 6hrs after lemon grass was done failed in near identical way to the Hynix MRDIMMs ( 15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ).  https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/5dfHHIaNk?orgId=1 RREL registers shows same 4DQ and around 32bit parity count and C4 Error class (same as MRDIMM idle fails) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/VlYsE4-Hz?orgId=1   same system failed back in Jan on a different dimm with same fail signature  @Lee, Caty let me know when the node is available.
Set SystemErrorEnable=0 and OS kernel parameter mcelog=off and let the node sit idle. System hit idle fails after ~10days of idle on separate dimm (CPU0 IMC5, SN 76C23D96) pythonsv logs attached fl31ca102gs0909_HynixRDimm-Renesas_Idle-CEStorm-CPU0IMC5_0612_pythonsv.zip Statusscope also captured 5e1bb603-26df-3ccf-4e0e-ac7b9b945985 - AxonSV - Record Viewer fail signature once again follows same 4DQ, 32 parity bit count, Error class C4 all Bank/bankgroup/Col/Row as the Hynix MRDimm idle issue as mentioned previously (15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/BzpX6EYHk?orgId=1  three different dimms have failed similarly in the past 6months on this node. Polling through historic data to see if there are more Hynix RDIMMs that have failed similarly.
There is strong evidence that the issue has been happening somewhat regularly on Hynix RDIMMs over the last 6 months. Repro rate is low and only two nodes have had repeated fails (though always on different dimms).  Below is the list of 4DQ fails in the cluster over the last 6 months. Each Vendor has ~4000-5000 dimms installed in the cluster

++++1566236212 kloh
will need node for repro dimm reported CE storm during idle, 6hrs after lemon grass was done failed in near identical way to the Hynix MRDIMMs ( 15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ).  https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/5dfHHIaNk?orgId=1 RREL registers shows same 4DQ and around 32bit parity count and C4 Error class (same as MRDIMM idle fails) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/VlYsE4-Hz?orgId=1   same system failed back in Jan on a different dimm with same fail signature  @Lee, Caty let me know when the node is available.

++++1566315808 kloh
Set SystemErrorEnable=0 and OS kernel parameter mcelog=off and let the node sit idle. System hit idle fails after ~10days of idle on separate dimm (CPU0 IMC5, SN 76C23D96) pythonsv logs attached fl31ca102gs0909_HynixRDimm-Renesas_Idle-CEStorm-CPU0IMC5_0612_pythonsv.zip Statusscope also captured 5e1bb603-26df-3ccf-4e0e-ac7b9b945985 - AxonSV - Record Viewer fail signature once again follows same 4DQ, 32 parity bit count, Error class C4 all Bank/bankgroup/Col/Row as the Hynix MRDimm idle issue as mentioned previously (15017625872 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR_AP B3][MRDIMM][Hynix MR + Renesas WW09 2024 ] MEM CE Storm on multipled dimms during idle ) https://grafana02.jf.sova.intel.com/goto/BzpX6EYHk?orgId=1  three different dimms have failed similarly in the past 6months on this node. Polling through historic data to see if there are more Hynix RDIMMs that have failed similarly.

++++1566325531 kloh
There is strong evidence that the issue has been happening somewhat regularly on Hynix RDIMMs over the last 6 months. Repro rate is low and only two nodes have had repeated fails (though always on different dimms).  Below is the list of 4DQ fails in the cluster over the last 6 months. Each Vendor has ~4000-5000 dimms installed in the cluster

articles.title: [SRF AP C0] y-cruncher workload standalone causes the system to Power off
articles.description:
Trying to reproduce the issue reported here: 22019812509 - [SRF AP C0][RAS]Unexpected address reported by bank 9 with CHA LLC Uncorrectable error (intel.com) it was found that by executing the workload even without error injection causes the system to power off. I have tried setting machine check and shutdown breakpoints but these haven't been reached in the reboot caused by the workload. This is the command used to execute the workload: y-cruncher
pause:-1 colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 This issue has been reproduced in three SRFAP systems
comments: The next first step will be to change from full Hardware Lockstep to disable Hardware Lockstep.
Even with Hardware Lockstep disabled, the system still reboots while the workload is executing. Next step is try to reproduce in SRF SP with 2 sockets.

If this is only happening on 1 station, you're most likely therm tripping or OCP, please get your system further checked That system should not be running any RAS-centric test until 1st sanitized & triaged
This has been seen in 3 SRF AP systems now, not seen in a  1S SRF SP. It's still pending to check if it's reproducible in GNR or 2S SRF SP.

Removing [RAS] from the tag,  SRF AP has a much higher power draw than SRF SP. It wouldn't surprise me that this is SRF AP only, please get this prioritized. This has nothing to do with RAS, but it means that you cannot run y-cruncher stress in 3 of the SRF-AP systems that you have tried. @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra @Gonzalez Perez, Luis is this a regression? Please tag accordingly I don't see this get reported before, and SRF-AP PO was months ago, is it truly the 1st time you run y-cruncher?

Trying to isolate this issue I have tried the following experiments: Executed overnight (~15 hours) y-cruncher with only one socket enabled ---> This test passed, the system didn't reboot. Executed with half of the cores disabled (288 cores enabled/288 cores disabled) distributed between 2 sockets ---> This test didn't cause the system to reboot but I was only able to execute 2 hours to continue with experiments during the day Right now I am executing with all cores enabled and monitoring some package temperature registers, I see the temperature increasing during the execution but this experiment is not concluded yet: The system in idle has values like this: sv.sockets.io0.uncore.punit.ptpcioregs.ptpcioregs.package_temperature.show() 0x0000005f : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow. 0x00000064 : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow. The system running the y-cruncher has values like this: sv.sockets.io0.uncore.punit.ptpcioregs.ptpcioregs.package_temperature.show() 0x0000008c : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow. 0x00000097 : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow.

@Magdaleno Millan, Marcela Please collab with Ale to check on BMC information to verify if there are any breadcrumbs on the Reboot reason. AR: @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra  to try to use monitoring data from BMC. systemctl stop com.intel.crashdump journalctl -ef -t power-control -t host-error-monitor -t host-misc-manager -t crashdump Is the BMC still up after reboot? (Ale believes that BMC is lost on this condition, need confirmation on this)

After system power of, we perform a power cycle in order to access to OpenBMC due the system lost BMC access we got this information from OpenBMC and Redfish EventLog event entries a : Memory Hi Team, Are you observing abnormal / big variation in fan PWM values during stress? Per BMC team, there has been a fan algorithm change in 24.13 which is contributing to thermal throttling & impacting the performance. Please refer 15015922644 - [Cluster][SRF-SP][C0][BKC77] FB5/Linpack/SPECcpu have perf drop up to ~6% on some nodes of Q4VY/Q4WS/Q4VX/Q4VZ compared with BKC75 results (intel.com) 14022089856 - [Cluster][FLEX GNR/SRF] Thermal Trip (post code 0x4a) Fan speeds down until 40% DTS/Die High Temp (intel.com) thank you Shashi Kiran [SRF Platform Sysdebug Lead]

@Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra reported this as Whereas Do actually flag this: So something is not right in this triage, please confirm & update accordingly. That is the importance of populating regression:YES properly, if this was a regression then I agree with @Belur, Shashi Kiran

We have tried to check if the issue reported here is the same issue reported by the Cluster team by continue using the BMC 24.13 and have found the following: This issue seems not to be related to the thermal trip reported by Cluster team, in the BMC journal there's no messages about reaching thresholds, thermal trips or fan speeds, I'm attaching the BMC log. I still have the problem of the BMC console powers off too so I can't read the post code. The memory thermal trip in the BMC events is shown in only one system but it appears every time the system is power cycled, no matter if it suddenly shutdowns or if we power it off using Raritan. In a second SRF AP system which is connected to a PDU along with several more systems, this issue is seen more frequently. With help from @Garcia Rodriguez, Diego and @Molina Sabido, Gerardo the actual suspicion is that the PDU has some limitation for the power needed by the systems, we have seen the system powering off when it reaches a high power consumption, there is still needed more experiments to confirm this. Also next experiments will be done with the new BMC version 24.16-2 to see if this helps to mitigate this issue.

It was confirmed that this issue is not related to fix in BMC 24.16-2. Even after having this BMC 24.16-2 version, the unexpected shutdowns are still seen. These are the experiments that have been done so far: In the Raritan settings it was increased the "RMS Current" threshold, for upper warning from 6.5A to 8.5A and for upper critical from 8A to 12A in 2 SRF AP systems and the unexpected shutdowns are still seen in both systems. I was probing one y-cruncher algorithm at time trying to check if the issue is related to a special algorithm and so far I have the following:  Algorithms CS17CA101DN1105 SR32DML001N0201 y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 BKT 8 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 BBP Fail at 2 iteration 5 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SFT Fail at 1st iteration Failed at 41 iteration y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SNT 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SVT 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 FFT Fail at 32 iteration  Fail at 21000 iteration (~7hr) y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 N63 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 VT3 Fail at 49 iteration   Today I had a chat with a Raritan expert from iVE, he told me this actually could be related to a thermo-magnetic circuit that is in the Raritan that could be causing the shutdown, he suggested me to ask for a load balancing to the lab, I will continue with the investigation on this Raritan matter.

Hello @Belur, Shashi Kiran  We need help in this HSD, our current suspicion points towards the occurrence of current spikes generated by the systems while running stress applications. It seems that the Power Distribution Unit (PDU) may be activating an auto-protecting mechanism, leading to unexpected shutdowns during the execution of high-stress applications, so far we haven't been able to catch these current spikes in the PDU event logs. Given that these events are logged every second, there's a possibility that these critical moments are not being captured, although they might indeed be occurring. In the PDU logs we can see the systems reaching 8A when executing these high stress apps and the PDUs they are connected to have outputs marked as 10A. This issue is blocking us in the debug of other issues since the instability it causes in systems only running workload tasks. Thanks, Alejandra

Hi @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra -  Is the issue reproducible on a different SUT that is connected to the same PDU with y-cruncher stress? Can you find out how the different algorithms impacting the power utilization on the SUT since your experiments indicate certain algorithms are passing the test? I can share our sysdebug SUT for a few days if you would like to try. Please utilize CS17CA101DN1003.gar.corp.intel.com and let me know when we can take the system back. I presume your test does not require any extra peripherals such as additional PCIe cards, HSBP with drives etc., as sysdebug host is a plain system with silicon and some DIMM. thank you
Adding @Garcia, Eduardo from Board team for help with this HSD. Hi Eduardo - can you please get us some help on triaging this system power off issue that's happening under cpu/mem stress? thank you
Are 2 PSUs connected to the failing system?

Hi @Belur, Shashi Kiran , we have reproduced the problem across various systems, each connected to different PDUs. Notably, the SFT algorithm is consistently failing in less than 10 minutes across the systems. I will be using the sysdebug system you generously provided, please note I will not require any peripherals. Hi @Garcia, Eduardo , would you happen to know if there's a method for me to inspect the PSUs connected to the system? Or is it necessary for me to file a ticket for lab assistance to perform this check?  Thank you.

From current HSD description this needs help outside of RAS Sysdebug Forum, @Belur, Shashi Kiran could you please help us to add this HSD to Platform sysdebug agenda to follow up on the resolution of this HSD? @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra would continue to own this HSD but requires wider scope for resolution. (Changed from Sysdebug.platform.ras to Sysdebug.platform). Thanks in advance @Belur, Shashi Kiran
In BMC, you can run this command: i2cdetect -y 7 If there are 2 PSUs, you will see something like in the red circle. If only one PSU then you'll see just one device in line 50
Thanks @Garcia, Eduardo , actually I don't see any number in two systems:

Ok, that might be because there is a known issue where the PMBUS is hanging and you might be hitting that bug in the PLD and PFR. Those were fixed and released in this week's BKC.  So, you might need to physically inspect if 2 PSUs are present in the failing systems or flash the latest BKC in one of those systems.

Thanks @Garcia, Eduardo I will update to the latest BKC in the systems. I couldn't reproduce the failure in the sysdebug system, the algorithm that typically fails in minutes on other systems managed to run smoothly for some hours in this sysdebug system. I realized that the sysdebug system operates at a slower frequency compared to the other systems we've been testing: System Frequency Current average while executing y-cruncher CS17CA101DN1003.gar.corp.intel.com (Sysdebug system) 1.2 GHz ~5.2 A CS17CA101DN1105.gar.corp.intel.com 2.2 GHz ~7.0 A SR32DML001N0201.gar.corp.intel.com 1.9 GHz ~6.8 A
After updating one of the systems with the BKC #14, we could read the number of PSUs: We only have one PSU

While discussing with @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra and @Garcia Rodriguez, Diego we came up with the idea of reducing the core frequency as a workaround to avoid hitting this issue while it continues under debug. I reduced the frequency from 2.6Ghz to 2Ghz and the system ran the WL with the worst-case algorithm (y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SFT) over 2h without hitting the issue. It its worth to mention that the system running at 2Gz does not surpass 5.5A of power consumption.  Iteration: 8,818  Total Elapsed Time: 9818.102 seconds  ( 2.727 hours ) Running SFT: Passed  Test Speed:  3.06 * 10^11  bits / sec Iteration: 8,819  Total Elapsed Time: 9819.164 seconds  ( 2.728 hours ) Running SFT: Passed  Test Speed:  2.98 * 10^11  bits / sec Iteration: 8,820  Total Elapsed Time: 9820.317 seconds  ( 2.728 hours )
Team - Could you arrange 2nd PSU for your hosts and rerun the tests to see if the test passes with the POR QDF frequency? thank you.

The recommendation to use 2 PSUs is due to the defined power budget for the system. From the Avenue city RPAS: Per offline discussion with Alejandra, it seems that the system failed after a power peak of +1400W, thus, 2 PSUs are needed.  As a reference, to calculate the power that a system is using and to see if its between the PSU power budget check here: Avenue City power budget

There are quite a lot of runs from SRF-AP not able to run where you suspect to be the same: 22019953510 [SRF AP C0][RAS]System hangs after run CHA SF/LLC Correctable Errors Vazquez Santos, Kevin p3-medium presighting 2024-04-22 10:37:52.0 rejected Birch Stream Platform SRF AP duplicate val_tools RAS Subsystem,RAS Sysdebug,XPIV_SS_RAS Given the notes below from system requirements by @Garcia, Eduardo  , can you please expedite getting the proper # of PSU's @Gonzalez Perez, Luis  , @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra  as this is impacting bug-finding and real RAS test coverage

We were in the process to install a second PSU in one of the systems, now that we have it we are executing the y-cruncher with the failing algorithm and the POR QDF frequency and it's working, it's almost 2 hours running without shutdowns, the power is being distributed in the two PSUs: The next step is to ask for install the second PSU in the rest of the SRF AP systems where we are executing.

Today, Eduardo and I were checking one of the systems, and we found that, roughly speaking, a system would need 1500W:   SRF AP 500W * 2 sockets     = 1000W 24 memory DIMMS               ~   350W Other low energy devices    ~   200W Total energy needed               ~1500W   In a system with these characteristics, there would be a margin of 100W, using a single PSU of 1600W and connected to a power line of 220-240V. According to Eduardo, we could take the risk and keep the systems with just one PSU, the team needs to decide.   On the other hand, we are in the midst of transitioning CPUs in our validation systems from VIS to ES2 parts, with this change, we have observed that shutdowns have not occurred in one of the systems after running 9 hours the stress test that had made the system fail before, having ES2 288c 500W CPUs and a single PSU, we can see the PDU reaching ~1700W, but the system has not shutdown.     We have tested the new ES2 parts in other two systems, however these systems have fewer cores than before (256c), and shutdowns have not occurred after several hours.

Hi all, I did some experiments using C0 VIS cpu and C0 ES2 cpu And I got these results:   Using CPU: Q4UM (VIS) 288 cores, 1 PSU, Kernel 6.6.21.4, BIOS: 31D97, BMC: bhs-24.17-0-gf7e15b-6fddef2 CPLD BKC: R15 I can see the issue in the beginning of the test I’ve checked the power consumption, I got 7.8A , when the system reaches it, the system turns off       In the other hand, using this: CPU: Q4XM (ES2) 288 cores, 1 PSU, Kernel 6.6.21.4, BIOS: 31D97, BMC: bhs-24.17-0-gf7e15b-6fddef2 CPLD BKC: R15 I can run y-cruncher for almost 22 hours without problems, the maximum power consumption was 7.5A

Correcting my comment from the sysdebug meeting, the core frequency does change between the VIS and ES2 parts. The VIS parts where the failure has been observed have a higher frequency. Additionally, it has been noted that even if it is a high-frequency VIS part, at 3GHz, with 2 PSUs it no longer shuts down.  System SR32DML002S0301  CS17CA101DS1201 CS17CA101DN0406 CS17CA101DS1105 SR32DML001N0201 QDF Q4UM (VIS) Q4XN (ES2) Q4XM (ES2) Q4XN (ES2) Q4UU (VIS) Functional Cores 288 256 288 256 288 CPU Frequency 3.2GHz 2.7GHz 2.6GHz 2.7GHz 3.0GHz Memory Type 6400 / DDR5 6400 / DDR5 6400 / DDR5 6400 / DDR5 6400 / DDR5 Memory Quantity 24 24 24 24 24 Memory DIMM Size 64 256 64 128 128 Total Memory 1536GB 6144GB 1536GB 3072GB 3072GB Storage 2TB 1TB 1TB 1TB 2TB PSUs installed 1 1 1 1 2

@Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra - have you confirmed that all of the failures seen so far were with only 1 PSU? If so, per Eduardo in id: 14612387160,  it is recommended that we should have 2 PSUs, therefore this is not a defect - please confirm. The effort of exploring the possibility of using 1 PSU on certain config should be tracked somewhere else.

Hi @Lu, Lyle it seems the failures are influenced by a combination of factors: the number of PSUs connected and the power required, which is reflected in the core frequency. The VIS parts with higher frequency require more power. According to @Garcia, Eduardo comment in id: 14612387160, we need to assess the power budget to determine the necessary number of PSUs. My concern, though, is not with a defect per se, but with the fact that we have tested both VIS and ES2 parts with SKUs rated at a TDP of 500, yet they seem to have different energy consumption levels. It seems that the power budget calculator is not accurately estimating the requirements for those parts with higher frequencies, @Garcia, Eduardo could you please provide us with your input?

+++per Eduardo: "Per offline discussion with Alejandra, it seems that the system failed after a power peak of +1400W, thus, 2 PSUs are needed. " +++your calculation that we need to support ~1500W with 500W TDP parts: Today, Eduardo and I were checking one of the systems, and we found that, roughly speaking, a system would need 1500W:   SRF AP 500W * 2 sockets     = 1000W 24 memory DIMMS               ~   350W Other low energy devices    ~   200W Total energy needed               ~1500W   I thought that means we need 2 PSUs for using these 500W TDP parts - is that correct?

Hi @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra , BDC Lab team has confirmed that BDC labs (SRR/CtrlS) offer 220V high line power source to the SUTs. Hence, with two PSUs, your config should run stress tests successfully. Please find the response below for the other queries. Is there an issue with the CPUs that causes them to consume more power than expected under high-stress conditions? CPU power consumption does increase as the stress increases. Otherwise, we may see performance issues/instructions not being serviced etc. But increase in power consumption cannot be termed as an issue. What could be an issue though, could be...the CPUs not reaching the advertised TDP under heavy load. I believe we are not seeing this "TDP not reaching the max limit" issue with this test case. Why do ES2 parts have a lower frequency compared to VIS parts? This could be based on the learnings from earlier stepping validation/issues. Si arch could cap the frequency on ES2 parts compared to VIS to work around/avoid potential hardware / sw/fw issues. I do not have the diff b/n VIS and ES2 parts other than the data in LIRA database. But generally, earlier stepping (VIS) would support higher frequencies. With ES2 parts, it seems we are on the threshold, nearly reaching 1700W, but so far, we haven't had any system with ES2 parts shut down after running tests for several days. With any part (VIS/ES2), if there is very less headroom with the available power/thermals under stress/load, risk of system going down any time would be very high though the system may be functioning somehow despite reaching the power/thermal threshold. As a mitigation plan, we could consider installing a second PSU for each system equipped with 500W CPUs. However, we need to determine if we have a sufficient number of PSUs available for all these systems. I believe there is already a thread with PVST/JIRA tickets with EVF to arrange second PSUs for high wattage requirement configs. Is there an issue with the CPUs that causes them to consume more power than expected under high-stress conditions? CPU power consumption does increase as the stress increases. Otherwise, we may see performance issues/instructions not being serviced etc. But increase in power consumption cannot be termed as an issue. TITLE: [SRF AP C0] y-cruncher workload standalone causes the system to Power off

DESCRIPTION:
Trying to reproduce the issue reported here: 22019812509 - [SRF AP C0][RAS]Unexpected address reported by bank 9 with CHA LLC Uncorrectable error (intel.com) it was found that by executing the workload even without error injection causes the system to power off. I have tried setting machine check and shutdown breakpoints but these haven't been reached in the reboot caused by the workload. This is the command used to execute the workload: y-cruncher
pause:-1 colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 This issue has been reproduced in three SRFAP systems

COMMENTS:
The next first step will be to change from full Hardware Lockstep to disable Hardware Lockstep.
Even with Hardware Lockstep disabled, the system still reboots while the workload is executing. Next step is try to reproduce in SRF SP with 2 sockets.
If this is only happening on 1 station, you're most likely therm tripping or OCP, please get your system further checked That system should not be running any RAS-centric test until 1st sanitized & triaged
This has been seen in 3 SRF AP systems now, not seen in a  1S SRF SP. It's still pending to check if it's reproducible in GNR or 2S SRF SP.
Removing [RAS] from the tag,  SRF AP has a much higher power draw than SRF SP. It wouldn't surprise me that this is SRF AP only, please get this prioritized. This has nothing to do with RAS, but it means that you cannot run y-cruncher stress in 3 of the SRF-AP systems that you have tried. @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra @Gonzalez Perez, Luis is this a regression? Please tag accordingly I don't see this get reported before, and SRF-AP PO was months ago, is it truly the 1st time you run y-cruncher?
Trying to isolate this issue I have tried the following experiments: Executed overnight (~15 hours) y-cruncher with only one socket enabled ---> This test passed, the system didn't reboot. Executed with half of the cores disabled (288 cores enabled/288 cores disabled) distributed between 2 sockets ---> This test didn't cause the system to reboot but I was only able to execute 2 hours to continue with experiments during the day Right now I am executing with all cores enabled and monitoring some package temperature registers, I see the temperature increasing during the execution but this experiment is not concluded yet: The system in idle has values like this: sv.sockets.io0.uncore.punit.ptpcioregs.ptpcioregs.package_temperature.show() 0x0000005f : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow. 0x00000064 : data (07:00) (ro/v) -- Package temperature in degrees (C) PLUS 64C to prevent underflow. We have tried to check if the issue reported here is the same issue reported by the Cluster team by continue using the BMC 24.13 and have found the following: This issue seems not to be related to the thermal trip reported by Cluster team, in the BMC journal there's no messages about reaching thresholds, thermal trips or fan speeds, I'm attaching the BMC log. I still have the problem of the BMC console powers off too so I can't read the post code. The memory thermal trip in the BMC events is shown in only one system but it appears every time the system is power cycled, no matter if it suddenly shutdowns or if we power it off using Raritan. In a second SRF AP system which is connected to a PDU along with several more systems, this issue is seen more frequently. With help from @Garcia Rodriguez, Diego and @Molina Sabido, Gerardo the actual suspicion is that the PDU has some limitation for the power needed by the systems, we have seen the system powering off when it reaches a high power consumption, there is still needed more experiments to confirm this. Also next experiments will be done with the new BMC version 24.16-2 to see if this helps to mitigate this issue.
It was confirmed that this issue is not related to fix in BMC 24.16-2. Even after having this BMC 24.16-2 version, the unexpected shutdowns are still seen. These are the experiments that have been done so far: In the Raritan settings it was increased the "RMS Current" threshold, for upper warning from 6.5A to 8.5A and for upper critical from 8A to 12A in 2 SRF AP systems and the unexpected shutdowns are still seen in both systems. I was probing one y-cruncher algorithm at time trying to check if the issue is related to a special algorithm and so far I have the following:  Algorithms CS17CA101DN1105 SR32DML001N0201 y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 BKT 8 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 BBP Fail at 2 iteration 5 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SFT Fail at 1st iteration Failed at 41 iteration y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SNT 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 SVT 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 FFT Fail at 32 iteration  Fail at 21000 iteration (~7hr) y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 N63 1 hr / Pass 1 hr / Pass y-cruncher pause:-1  colors:0 stress -M:16G -D:1 VT3 Fail at 49 iteration   Today I had a chat with a Raritan expert from iVE, he told me this actually could be related to a thermo-magnetic circuit that is in the Raritan that could be causing the shutdown, he suggested me to ask for a load balancing to the lab, I will continue with the investigation on this Raritan matter.
Hello @Belur, Shashi Kiran  We need help in this HSD, our current suspicion points towards the occurrence of current spikes generated by the systems while running stress applications. It seems that the Power Distribution Unit (PDU) may be activating an auto-protecting mechanism, leading to unexpected shutdowns during the execution of high-stress applications, so far we haven't been able to catch these current spikes in the PDU event logs. Given that these events are logged every second, there's a possibility that these critical moments are not being captured, although they might indeed be occurring. Hi @Victoria Alcaraz, Alejandra , BDC Lab team has confirmed that BDC labs (SRR/CtrlS) offer 220V high line power source to the SUTs. Hence, with two PSUs, your config should run stress tests successfully. Please find the response below for the other queries. Is there an issue with the CPUs that causes them to consume more power than expected under high-stress conditions? CPU power consumption does increase as the stress increases. Otherwise, we may see performance issues/instructions not being serviced etc. But increase in power consumption cannot be termed as an issue. What could be an issue though, could be...the CPUs not reaching the advertised TDP under heavy load. I believe we are not seeing this "TDP not reaching the max limit" issue with this test case. Why do ES2 parts have a lower frequency compared to VIS parts? This could be based on the learnings from earlier stepping validation/issues. Si arch could cap the frequency on ES2 parts compared to VIS to work around/avoid potential hardware / sw/fw issues. I do not have the diff b/n VIS and ES2 parts other than the data in LIRA database. But generally, earlier stepping (VIS) would support higher frequencies. With ES2 parts, it seems we are on the threshold, nearly reaching 1700W, but so far, we haven't had any system with ES2 parts shut down after running tests for several days. With any part (VIS/ES2), if there is very less headroom with the available power/thermals under stress/load, risk of system going down any time would be very high though the system may be functioning somehow despite reaching the power/thermal threshold. As a mitigation plan, we could consider installing a second PSU for each system equipped with 500W CPUs. However, we need to determine if we have a sufficient number of PSUs available for all these systems. I believe there is already a thread with PVST/JIRA tickets with EVF to arrange second PSUs for high wattage requirement configs. articles.title: [GNR A0 PO][SRF A0 PO][Security] Linux Kernel boot not aware of TME AES-XTS-256 - x86/tme: Unknown policy is active & x86/mktme: No known encryption algorithm is supported
comments: Looking at the BIOS knobs kernel is reflecting what kernel is printing. TME enabled by BIOS: MKTME enabled by BIOS: And AES-XTS-256 algorithm enabled by default: Looks like the issue here is that the kernel doesn't know what to do when AES-XTS-256 algorithm is enabled

Booting with AES-XTS-128 algorithm system is not landing in to the errors seen with AES-XTS-256 [root@JF530NOR16BN0202T ~]# dmesg | grep tme [    2.177690] Initmem setup node 0 [mem 0x0000000000001000-0x000000207fffffff] [    4.605298] rcu: RCU calculated value of scheduler-enlistment delay is 100 jiffies. [    4.842911] x86/tme: enabled by BIOS [    4.843900] x86/mktme: enabled by BIOS [    4.844900] x86/mktme: 63 KeyIDs available [   34.401801] Freeing unused kernel image (initmem) memory: 2932K Adding @Chen, Tim C and @Sun, Yannan to help us getting more inputs from kernel and security sides.

From MSR perspective, the value is correct. 0x4 means the crypo algorithm is AES-256.   @Chen, Tim C The default cryptographic algorithm for MKTME is AES-128 w/o integrity on SPR and has been changed to AES-256 w/o integrity on GNR (FR: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14017005550) Looks like there is some gap in the implementation. Run itp.threads[0].msr(0x982) [64b] 0x000100060000000B BHS note: [64b] 0x000400060000002B Bit [0] should be set, indicating MSR 0x982 latched. Bit [1] should be set, indicating TME enabled. Bits [7:4] should be 0x2, indicating crypto algorithm is AES_XTS_256 (this is the default option if usrs did not set). Bits [51:48] should be 0x4, indicating crypto algorithm is AES_XTS_256 without integrity (this is the default option if uses did not set).

Another question, how does kernel handle TDX with respect to the dependency on MKTME? MKTME enablement is a pre-condition for TDX enabling, TDX works fine right now. Not sure if TDX enabling in kernel is based on the value of MSR 0x982 or the mktme_status in the code in description.

Checked with our TME developer Alison Schofield.  The message is purely cosmetic and informational and does not affect TME operation. There are plan in place to remove the warning.  And mktme_status is not used anywhere in the kernel.
Hao, can you answer Yannan's question " how does kernel handle TDX with respect to the dependency on MKTME? MKTME enablement is a pre-condition for TDX enabling"
Kernel tdx code will check MSR_IA32_MKTME_KEYID_PARTITIONING (0x00000087).
JIRA ticket to track this issue in Linux database is created: https://jira.devtools.intel.com/browse/LFE-6447
How to verify the message will not affect actual TME behavior with AES-256? Once confirmed, we would lower the priority.

You can do a grep of mktme_status in kernel code and see that it is not checked by any other code in Linux kernel.  Also confirmed by Hao that the key kernel component TDX depending on SGX does not use this but check msr directly.  There is work in progress by Alison to clean up and remove mktme_status entirely for upstream kernel.
ok thanks Tim, Keep open to track the cleanup, lower to P4.
Low priority, let linux team track it in JIRA.
Low priority, but we are still wanting this get fixed.
@Avelar, Omar @Wanyan, Feiting Are you still tracking this issue? I don't have access to the JIRA. So pls. update if there's plan to address this issue from kernel team.
One of the obstacles in posting a fix for this upstream is testing it. Please let me know when a GNR system, demonstrating the problem, is available for loan.

raw.description:
Summary:

Linux Kernel seems to only be aware of TME_ACTIVATE_POLICY_AES_XTS_128 and GNR is using AES-XTS-256 for MKTME by default.

Linux boots with pr_err and ultimately leaves mktme_status = MKTME_DISABLED;


Description:

Planned RAS tests involving TME encountered the following during enabling, which seems to be cosmetic but we still need this sorted out.


root@JF530NOR16BN0202T ~]# dmesg | grep tme

[    2.177389] Initmem setup node 0 [mem 0x0000000000001000-0x000000207fffffff]

[    4.606806] rcu: RCU calculated value of scheduler-enlistment delay is 100 jiffies.

[    4.843342] x86/tme: enabled by BIOS

[    4.844332] x86/tme: Unknown policy is active: 0x2

[    4.845333] x86/mktme: No known encryption algorithm is supported: 0x4

[    4.846335] x86/mktme: enabled by BIOS

[    4.847332] x86/mktme: 63 KeyIDs available

[   34.376046] Freeing unused kernel image (initmem) memory: 2932K


Which comes from /arch/x86/kernel/cpu/intel.c.


	tme_policy = TME_ACTIVATE_POLICY(tme_activate);
	if (tme_policy != TME_ACTIVATE_POLICY_AES_XTS_128)
		pr_warn("x86/tme: Unknown policy is active: %#llx\n", tme_policy);

	tme_crypto_algs = TME_ACTIVATE_CRYPTO_ALGS(tme_activate);
	if (!(tme_crypto_algs & TME_ACTIVATE_CRYPTO_AES_XTS_128)) {
		pr_err("x86/mktme: No known encryption algorithm is supported: %#llx\n",
				tme_crypto_algs);
		mktme_status = MKTME_DISABLED;
	}


This was seen in Intel-next 5.19.0-gnr.po.bkc.1.1.2.x86_64 and also present in upstream with a code inspection from /arch/x86/kernel/cpu/intel.c.



The sillicon has the following setting


[root@JF530NOR16BN0202T fisher]# rdmsr -0 0x982
0x000400060000002b
:
In [152]: sv.sockets.soc.memss.mc0.ch0.mse.mse_activate.mse_policy.getspec()
##########################################################################################################################
# FIELD: mse_policy
# Attribute: rw
# UpperBit: 7
# LowerBit: 4
# CurrentValue: 2
# Description:
# 0000 - AES_XTS-128, 0001 - AES_XTS-128 with Integrity, 0010 - AES-XTS-256, 0011 - AES_XTS-256 with Integrity

raw.subject: bug
raw.server_platf.bug.root_cause_detail:
MKTME detection was added in anticipation of full kernel support
that never followed. Aside from just good housekeeping, this
cleanup is inspired by users who are confused by the TME/MKTME
messaging during boot.

From MSR perspective, the value is correct. 0x4 means the crypo algorithm is AES-256.   @Chen, Tim C The default cryptographic algorithm for MKTME is AES-128 w/o integrity on SPR and has been changed to AES-256 w/o integrity on GNR (FR: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/14017005550) Looks like there is some gap in the implementation. Bits [7:4] should be 0x2, indicating crypto algorithm is AES_XTS_256 (this is the default option if usrs did not set). Bits [51:48] should be 0x4, indicating crypto algorithm is AES_XTS_256 without integrity (this is the default option if uses did not set).

articles.title: [GNR A0 PO][X1][X3][RAS_DM] [2S] UPI CRC error is not reported at OS if previous error happens in a different port
articles.description: Very few errors are reported at OS level after performing CRC injections randomizing the UPI ports 2022.12 telemetry: unique entry = a91c9e287d0711edb31fa4bf018cc9a2 [01:16:16.777] I: fisher: stats: PASS = 9 - FAIL = 11 After some experiments was found that: 1. Errors are reported if are injected back to back in the same port 2. When a second error is injected in a different port the error is logged in kti_mc_st but not at OS level.
comments: Hi Diego, Does this TC passed with 1S? A 2S issue reported from silicon. Maybe it's worth having a try with PYSV workaround.  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- From: Fausto, Matthew B Sent: Tuesday, December 20, 2022 2:06 PM To: GNR VST Cc: Fausto, Matthew B Subject: GNR Val: To all teams doing 2Skt debug - upi routing table issue - PYSV code being verified then to be cloned to BIOS Feature   If you are involved in any 2Skt execution, please note this sighting and the UPI Routing Table updates.  Once enough cycles to verify it is good, this will be root-caused to a BIOS Feature for implementation.   So if you are doing 2Skt debug, please try these PYSV settings.     [GNR A0 PO][X1][2S] Seeing Core Data Error on 2 socket platform for DWr thread with D2K enabled https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16018792887/main

Hi @Wanyan, Feiting this scenario is not applicable for 1S platforms as is injection in the UPI link, so first steps will be to see if the problem with the injection is coming from an specific UPI port or injector response. Worth to mention that logic is ported from EGS where injection flow used to work all the time
Oh, it's UPI, my fault. Let's start from error log analysis. Thanks Diego!
@Garcia Rodriguez, Diego what's the latest status of this TC?
Low injection rate is worst in X3. telemetry: entry = 2023.02/e43a41dfa5ce11ed87ca0242ac110002 Will collect the injector parameters in order to look for a pattern in failing and  passing cases.

With current data, it seems this is unique to X1/X3. Running on 2S X2 with current UPI topology this issue is NOT shown.  Currently running (still in progress) : telemetry: entry = 2023.02/447d87a8a74f11ed90a80007e9342bdf [root@gnr-bkc UPI_CRC_Injection]# dmidecode | grep BHS         Version: BHSDCRB1.SYS.0020.D30.2301201241 As of now: 24 successful cycles UPI topology is:  import graniterapids.upi.upiStatus as upis upis.printTopology -------> upis.printTopology() 2S4Q Topology S0_P0 S1_P1 S0_P1 S1_P0 S0_P2 S1_P2 S0_P3 S1_P3 S1_P0 S0_P1 S1_P1 S0_P0 S1_P2 S0_P2 S1_P3 S0_P3 -------------       ------------- |          3*********3          | |          2*********2          | |     0     |       |     1     | |          1*********0          | |          0*********1          | -------------       -------------

I have been performing several experiments to try to isolate the failure. This experiments has happened in a X1 and X3 system in parallel: [1] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and fixed parameters in einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry - PASS [2] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode - PASS [3] Injecting in upi port 0 (socket0, io0) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry- PASS [4] Injecting in upi port 5 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL [5]Injecting in upi port 2 (socket0, io1) and randomizing einjretryactivemode and einjnumretry-FAIL At this point we can confirm that the injector parameters are correct and the suspicion was that the ports in io1 were the ones presenting the issue but after injecting back to port0 the errors are not been seen at OS level. Looking at the injector it shows that the error was injected: In [22]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst Out[22]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 Also I do see that upi mca has logged the errors in the ports where the errors were not seen at OS level. In [23]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.kti_mc_st Out[23]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800034000300e0f socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800014000300e0f socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800010000300e0f socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x8800010000300e0f socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi4.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 socket1.io1.uncore.upi.upi5.upi_regs.kti_mc_st - 0x0000000000000000 Could it be an override rules problem? I found a pattern in this failure: All the ports has been injected the error successfully In [42]: sv.sockets.ios.uncore.upi.upis.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst Out[42]: socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi0.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 2nd injected port  socket0.io0.uncore.upi.upi1.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000001 1st injected port socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi2.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - 0x00000000 socket0.io1.uncore.upi.upi3.upi_regs.ktirxeinjctl0.errinjst - TITLE: [GNR A0 PO][X1][X3][RAS_DM] [2S] UPI CRC error is not reported at OS if previous error happens in a different port

DESCRIPTION:

raw.server_platf.bug.suspect_area_reason: MCA reporting of UPI error banks
raw.server_platf.bug.root_cause_detail: Since internal UPI agent mapping for UPI4 and UPI5 are not correctly configured, after CRC error injection to UPI ports, errors are reported as if they are injected back to back in the same port.  Also, when a second error is injected in a different port the error is logged in kti_mc_st but it's not reported at OS level.

articles.title: [GNR A1][RAS_DM] CsmiDynamicDisable is incorrectly enabled by default by BIOS
articles.description: It was agreed for Servers back in 2021 during RAS WG that the default for CsmiDynamicDisable should be set to disabled for SPR and beyond (while a UBOX thresholding scheme is decided that doesn't disable SMI's forever). But we should not be masking of CSMI's forever per MCi_BANK. Current BHS BIOS builds are not honoring that func_requirement here https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16013180336 and breaks the agreement since BHS and next-gens were also marked as affected. While the default is still enabled in BirchStream UEFI images: CLI command executed successfully.. BIOS knobs CLI Command ended successfully , see below for the results.. |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| |VI|Ofset| Knob Name |Sz| DefVal | CurVal | |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| | 3| 009F| CsmiDynamicDisable| 1| 1 | 1 | |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| Verify Fail: Knob = CsmiDynamicDisable ExpectedVal = 0x0 CurrVal = 0x1
comments: @Annam, Krishna V are you aware of the background as to why https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16013180336 did not carry forward for BHS GNR?
Hi Omar, We found that it was miss in updating the default value in GNR setup file for CsmiDynamicDisable. Please clone to bios sighting.

TITLE: [GNR A1][RAS_DM] CsmiDynamicDisable is incorrectly enabled by default by BIOS

DESCRIPTION:
It was agreed for Servers back in 2021 during RAS WG that the default for CsmiDynamicDisable should be set to disabled for SPR and beyond (while a UBOX thresholding scheme is decided that doesn't disable SMI's forever). But we should not be masking of CSMI's forever per MCi_BANK. Current BHS BIOS builds are not honoring that func_requirement here https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16013180336 and breaks the agreement since BHS and next-gens were also marked as affected. While the default is still enabled in BirchStream UEFI images: CLI command executed successfully.. BIOS knobs CLI Command ended successfully , see below for the results.. |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| |VI|Ofset| Knob Name |Sz| DefVal | CurVal | |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| | 3| 009F| CsmiDynamicDisable| 1| 1 | 1 | |--|-----|------------------------------------------|--|-----------|-----------| Verify Fail: Knob = CsmiDynamicDisable ExpectedVal = 0x0 CurrVal = 0x1

@Annam, Krishna V are you aware of the background as to why https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16013180336 did not carry forward for BHS GNR?

articles.title: [RAS_DM][CXL] CXL.MEM correctable errors OS error handling is incomplete in OSFM
articles.description: This issue was seen in previously in EGS platforms: [EMR][SPR][CXL] CXL.MEM error handling and signaling incomplete in OS First Mode with CXL 1.0 The problem is the following: When a CXL.MEM error happens in OSFM the error handler only attends the error in the RCEC keeping the error logged in the CXL AER register when this register is not cleared a CXL Root Port is not sending new AER messages to IEH unless the previous error is cleared. The handling is matching the specification: https://docs.intel.com/documents/iparch/cxlcm/HAS/Gen4/features/IPCXL-223/IPCXL_223_FHAS.html#reliability-availability-and-serviceability-ras-4 Error Flow DP A .io logs errors in local AER Ext Cap (in RCRB) DP A .cache & .mem logs errors in Mem Space registers DP A .cache, .mem, or .io sends PCIe AER msg with .io block Src Port ID on SB to Sat IEH B Sat IEH B logs received PCIe AER msg in single Local Error register (same Src Port ID) Sat IEH B logs UIE/CIE in RCEC Sat IEH B logs source (RCEC) in Global Error Sat IEH B generates PCIe Error msg on SB to Gbl IEH With own ReqID and strapped Bitmap OS Error Handling Inspect and handle RCEC AER FW Error Handling Inspect Gbl IEH Global Error Inspect Sat IEH Global Error Inspect RCEC AER and Local Error Inspect DP AER & handle Mem (or Cache, IO) errors But this flow has to be enhanced to complete a successful error handling in the CXL root port.

I noticed the subject line changed... Technically OSFM doesn't handle uncorrectable errors either. RCEC sees a UIE, but OS doesn't go the CXL.CM and read uncorrectable error status register either. It's just less obvious because the OS usually doesn't survive. Need to study the not reporting issue.  Loosing future errors is acceptable as seen by. https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/22016951635 If we had a full OSFM handling or even FFM, we could have a race condition where. - Read RCEC (UIE/CIE) - Read CXL.CM - Clear CXL.CM <-- New CXL.CM error comes in (Will a new interrupt be triggered, because RCEC UIE/CIE hasn't been cleared yet?) - Clear RCEC  Results will be - RCEC Clear <== even if a new interrupt was sent, normal code would stop at RCEC because UIE/CIE = 0. - CXL.CM has error <== prevents future errors from interrupting? We would need an algorithm like - Read RCEC (UIE/CIE) - Clear RCEC  - Read CXL.CM - Clear CXL.CM <-- New CXL.CM error comes in (will trigger new UIE/CIE and hopefully trigger an interrupt) Heavily tested and documented. Otherwise we end up with 22016951635 again.

comments_structured.author: etsaur
comments_structured.text: I noticed the subject line changed... Technically OSFM doesn't handle uncorrectable errors either. RCEC sees a UIE, but OS doesn't go the CXL.CM and read uncorrectable error status register either. It's just less obvious because the OS usually doesn't survive. Need to study the not reporting issue.  Loosing future errors is acceptable as seen by. https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/22016951635 If we had a full OSFM handling or even FFM, we could have a race condition where. - Read RCEC (UIE/CIE) - Read CXL.CM - Clear CXL.CM <-- New CXL.CM error comes in (Will a new interrupt be triggered, because RCEC UIE/CIE hasn't been cleared yet?) - Clear RCEC  Results will be - RCEC Clear <== even if a new interrupt was sent, normal code would stop at RCEC because UIE/CIE = 0. - CXL.CM has error <== prevents future errors from interrupting? We would need an algorithm like - Read RCEC (UIE/CIE) - Clear RCEC  - Read CXL.CM - Clear CXL.CM <-- New CXL.CM error comes in (will trigger new UIE/CIE and hopefully trigger an interrupt) Heavily tested and documented. Otherwise we end up with 22016951635 again.
